invariants_verified: The RBAC policy and role-operation matrix are versioned and reject unsupported policy versions.
Authorization resolves the server-supplied principal identity and requires an exact tenant, organisation, project and environment scope match.
Proposal and approval authority are separate; a proposer cannot approve their own proposal.
Machine credentials are issued only to machine principals, store a SHA-256 digest rather than the raw secret, and bind to one environment.
Credential authentication rejects wrong secrets, revoked credentials, expired credentials and cross-environment use.
Credential rotation revokes the current credential and issues a replacement with an incremented version.
The local outbox worker derives deterministic effect identity, fences competing leases, supports same-owner renewal and recovers expired claims.
Effect replay and retry paths produce validated canonical receipts with verifiable integrity digests.
The local worker tests cover fault points before and after simulated effects without claiming external exactly-once provider effects.
limitations: This evidence proves only a local TypeScript RBAC, machine-credential and filesystem outbox-worker slice.
No CI execution, staging identity provider, hosted identity service, hosted RBAC enforcement, RLS, trusted operator identity or production credential evidence is available.

The local outbox worker does not prove disposable database/queue transactionality, claim-lease workers, cross-process concurrency, reconciliation-before-retry, or exactly-once external provider effects.
The current local retryable-failure path remains a bounded simulator behavior and does not establish provider acceptance or unknown-outcome reconciliation.
No provider sandbox, staging, production, billing settlement, capacity, commercial readiness or whole-product certification is claimed.
verdict: ATLAS-BMR2-P6-002 = BLOCKED_EXTERNAL / LOCAL_PROVEN — local versioned RBAC, exact scope, separated proposal/approval authority, environment-bound digest-only machine credentials, rotation/revocation, and bounded local outbox receipt integrity are proven; CI, staging identity-provider and hosted enforcement evidence remain unavailable.
